elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: The operative sentence now reads: "Customer may obtain those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2, from M&I or from any other provider, and shall have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation." The mandatory "shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services" language and the "during the Term" lock-in are gone; the retained first sentence is a pricing acknowledgement only and imposes no sourcing duty. Deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" is ok, and the rationale confirms other "exclusive" hits (§ 17.1, § 21.7(A), § 22, § 23, § 21.10) are not Customer-side sourcing obligations.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no exclusivity obligation binds Customer at all, so there is no scope needing category limitation. The condition to which this element attaches (an existing exclusivity) does not apply.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the eight-year "during the Term" lock-in has been deleted and replaced with permissive sourcing, so there is no exclusivity period of any length to cap.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity survives that would need a service-level exit; Customer is free at all times to source from any other provider. Note the comment only offers this as a negotiating fallback, it is not in operative text — which is acceptable because the stronger preferred position is achieved.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied for the same reason: there is no residual exclusivity to terminate on delivery-date failure, so no delivery-date exit mechanic is required.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment. The mandatory sourcing obligation ("shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services ... during the Term") is fully removed and replaced with an affirmative right to source from M&I or any other provider.

Minimality holds: only the second sentence of § 10.3(A) was touched. The favourable/neutral first-sentence pricing acknowledgement, the cross-reference to Schedule 6.2 and the defined term "Monthly Base Fee" are all retained verbatim. No survival tail, expense allocation, remedy, procedure or extra requirement outside the EXCLUSIVITY checklist was added.

The closing phrase "and shall have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation" is mildly belt-and-suspenders alongside "from M&I or from any other provider," but it states the target element itself rather than adding a term outside the checklist, so it does not break minimality. If the drafter wants the tightest possible edit, that trailing clause could be dropped.

Intent is preserved: the pricing rationale sentence survives without contradiction (it is an acknowledgement, not a covenant), Schedule 6.2 remains the reference for the scope of Monthly Base Fee Services, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling. Existing § 9 service credits and § 12 default remedies are untouched, so unrelated remedies and commercial mechanics survive.

Correctly scoped to the customer side: the redline does not disturb exclusivity that benefits Customer, and does not re-flag § 17.1 Customer Data ownership, § 22 venue or § 23 licence grant, which are not Customer sourcing obligations.

Practical note for negotiation only (no repair required): because the pricing acknowledgement in the first sentence survives, M&I may argue the Monthly Base Fee assumes full sourcing volume and seek a price adjustment if Customer descopes. If that risk matters commercially, consider pairing the edit with confirmation that Schedule 6.2 pricing is not repriced on partial sourcing — but that is outside this checklist and should not be added here without failing minimality.
